Frequently asked questions
Quick answers about using your phone as a wireless gamepad, keyboard & mouse, TV remote, and presentation controller. For step-by-step setup, see the How-to guide. Download PocketPad on Google Play.
Getting started
How can I use my phone as a gamepad or game controller?

Install PocketPad on your Android phone from Google Play. Open a gamepad layout (Xbox-style or PlayStation-style), connect via Bluetooth HID (no app on your PC) or Wi‑Fi with PocketPad Companion on Windows, then play. Your phone sends real gamepad input — sticks, triggers, D-pad, and face buttons.
How do I use my phone as a remote keyboard and mouse for my PC?

In PocketPad, select the Universal layout (touchpad + typing panel). Connect over Bluetooth HID or Wi‑Fi. You get pointer movement, scrolling, WASD clusters, full keyboard typing, and shortcuts like Ctrl+C and Alt+Tab.
Can I use my phone as a TV remote control?

Yes. Use the Media Remote layout with volume, play/pause, skip, and D-pad keys. Pair your phone to a Smart TV, Android TV, Fire TV, or PC via Bluetooth HID and control Netflix, YouTube, Plex, VLC, Kodi, and other apps.
How can I use my phone as a presentation or slide controller?

Open the Slide Controller layout. Swipe to advance or go back in PowerPoint, Google Slides, Keynote, or Canva. Buttons cover fullscreen, black screen, and white screen. Bluetooth HID works with no install on the presenter laptop.
Does PocketPad work without installing anything on my PC?

Yes — Bluetooth HID mode needs zero software on the host. Pair from Windows, Mac, Linux, Android, or TV Bluetooth settings. For lowest latency and multiplayer on Windows, optionally install the free PocketPad Companion desktop app.
How do I connect PocketPad instantly via Bluetooth?

1) Install PocketPad on Android. 2) In the app, choose Bluetooth transport and tap Prepare for pairing. 3) On your PC/Mac/TV, open Bluetooth settings → Add device → select your phone. 4) In PocketPad, pick a layout and start controlling. See the How-to guide for details.
How do I connect PocketPad over Wi‑Fi with Companion?

1) Install PocketPad Companion on Windows (installer EXE from the overview page). 2) Allow private network access in Windows Firewall. 3) Put phone and PC on the same Wi‑Fi. 4) Open Companion, then in PocketPad tap Connect and choose your PC. 5) For Universal keyboard/mouse, enter the 6-digit code from Companion Settings.
Connection & performance
Should I use Bluetooth or Wi‑Fi to connect PocketPad?

Bluetooth HID is fastest to set up — pair once, no PC install, works on Mac/Linux/TV. Wi‑Fi + Companion is best on Windows when you want auto-discovery, a pairing code for Universal layouts, the lowest jitter, and multiple phones at once.
How low is PocketPad's latency?

Bluetooth HID is tuned for responsive gaming; Wi‑Fi through Companion is optimized for LAN with very low jitter. Keep devices on the same Wi‑Fi band and wake sleeping PCs — Bluetooth radios may pause until the host is active.
Can I use my phone as a gamepad without a server app on my computer?

Yes. PocketPad's Bluetooth HID mode registers your phone as a standard Bluetooth gamepad, keyboard, or mouse — unlike DroidJoy, Monect, or PC Remote which require a desktop server. No drivers or background apps on the host.
Can multiple phones connect as controllers at the same time?

Yes. Over Wi‑Fi with PocketPad Companion on Windows, several phones can connect to one PC. Each phone appears as a separate Xbox controller (Gamepad 1, 2, 3…) for couch co-op without buying extra physical pads.
Does PocketPad work with Steam and PC games?

Yes. Over Bluetooth HID or Companion (virtual Xbox controller via ViGEm), games that support standard Xbox controllers should recognize PocketPad. Use a gamepad layout for controller-native games; use Universal WASD + mouse for titles that expect keyboard and mouse.
Does PocketPad work on Mac and Linux?
Yes for Bluetooth HID — pair from macOS or Linux Bluetooth settings with no Companion install. The Windows Companion app is only for Wi‑Fi/virtual gamepad on Windows.
Can I control a Smart TV or Android TV with PocketPad?

Yes, when the TV accepts Bluetooth HID keyboards or remotes. Use Media Remote or Universal layouts. Some TVs route Bluetooth audio oddly — disable phone media audio in Bluetooth settings if the TV mutes speakers.
Troubleshooting
My PC doesn't show PocketPad in Bluetooth — what should I try?

In PocketPad, tap Prepare for pairing before scanning on the PC. Remove old pairings for your phone in both devices' Bluetooth lists. On Windows, use Add device → Bluetooth. Switching gamepad vs keyboard mode usually requires re-pairing.
PocketPad won't connect over Wi‑Fi — firewall help?
Allow PocketPad Companion on private networks when Windows Firewall prompts. Phone and PC must be on the same subnet. Guest Wi‑Fi isolation blocks discovery — use the main LAN.
My game doesn't recognize PocketPad as a controller

Confirm you are in a gamepad layout (not Universal keyboard mode). On Windows Wi‑Fi, ensure Companion is running and ViGEmBus is installed. Some games only support XInput — use Companion on Windows for virtual Xbox pads.
Why do I need to pair again after switching layouts or modes?

Bluetooth HID uses different device profiles for gamepad vs keyboard/mouse composite. Most operating systems require a fresh pairing when PocketPad switches HID registration. Follow Prepare for pairing each time you change transport or major layout class.
Why does Windows Companion mention ViGEmBus?

Windows games expect Xbox-style controllers. Companion uses the open-source ViGEm stack so your phone appears as a virtual Xbox pad. The installer adds ViGEmBus only if it is not already on your PC (e.g. from DS4Windows).
App, privacy & billing
What is the best app to use my phone as a wireless game controller?

PocketPad is an all-in-one option: gamepad, keyboard & mouse, TV/media remote, and slide controller in one app. It supports Bluetooth HID (no server) and Wi‑Fi with Companion, custom layouts, tilt-to-steer, and multiple phones on one PC.
Do I need an account to use PocketPad?
No. PocketPad works without sign-in. Layouts and settings stay on your device. Optional anonymous analytics can be declined on first launch in regions that require consent.
Does PocketPad work offline?
Yes. Bluetooth control and local Wi‑Fi to Companion do not require internet. Only optional analytics, ads (free tier), and Play Store purchases need connectivity.
Is PocketPad free? What is PocketPad Pro?

PocketPad is free to download with core controller features. PocketPad Pro (Google Play) removes ads and unlocks cosmetic skins. Purchases are handled by Google Play — PocketPad does not store payment details.
Does PocketPad collect my controller inputs or layouts?

PocketPad does not send live controller inputs, layouts, or screen content to Datron servers. Optional anonymous Firebase Analytics and Crashlytics apply only if you opt in (or default-on outside the EU/UK/CH). See the Privacy Policy.
Can I customize button layouts and create my own presets?
Yes. PocketPad includes a drag-and-edit layout editor — resize and move sticks, buttons, triggers, and D-pad zones. Copy built-in presets, save profiles, and switch between them per game or task.
Can I steer racing games with phone tilt?
Yes. PocketPad supports tilt-to-steer on gamepad layouts — map device orientation to steering input for racing titles that accept gamepad axes.
Is PocketPad the same as the Pocket-Pad app on GitHub?

No. PocketPad by Datron (com.datron.pocketpad) is a separate product with keyboard/mouse, TV remote, slide controller, custom layouts, Wi‑Fi Companion, and Pro on Google Play. Unrelated open-source projects may share a similar name but are not affiliated with Datron.
